summary: A Depth subscription on an NFO future: after the dk snapshot a df sends every bid level as price 0 and quantity 0, then a df restores five bids.

notes: The desktop takes a level sent with price 0 and quantity 0 in a df as gone and publishes the bid side empty; the web drops levels without a price and keeps the previous side when none is left (aliceblue_adapter.py:700-718). A df carries only the keys that changed, so a sent 0 is a value: the web's kept side is ghost liquidity (lead ruling 2026-11-09, audit appendix item 10). Listed for the maintainer's live check.

deviations.reason: The web's Depth timestamp is AliceBlue's feed time ft as it came, a string of epoch seconds; the frame timestamp is epoch milliseconds as a number (docs/prompt/websockets-format.md). The desktop sends the receipt time.

The web's Depth has no ltt: it puts AliceBlue's feed time, as a string of epoch seconds, in timestamp instead (aliceblue_mapping.py:255, aliceblue_adapter.py:1295-1300). The desktop sends the trade time as ltt in ms and its receipt time as timestamp, as every frame does.

AliceBlue's depth packet carries volume and the web's Depth dict leaves it out, sending only ltp, timestamp and the book (aliceblue_adapter.py:1270-1300): market data the broker sent, lost (lead ruling 2026-11-09). The desktop's Depth frame keeps it, as docs/api/websocket-streaming/depth.md shows the quote beside the book.

AliceBlue's dk and df carry each level's order count (bo1..bo5, so1..so5); the web publishes 0 for every level (aliceblue_adapter.py:1280-1290), a wrong value (lead ruling 2026-11-09). The desktop sends the counts. And a df that sends a level's price and quantity as 0 removes it; the web keeps the previous bids, a stale book (lead ruling 2026-11-09, audit appendix item 10; maintainer live check listed).
